expectations.text: Output contains valid YAML frontmatter with title, description, sidebar_position, and skills/objectives fields
expectations.evidence: YAML frontmatter present with title 'The Feedback Loop', description, sidebar_position: 5, skills array (2 entries: Thinking Self-Evaluation, Feedback Loop Construction), learning_objectives array (2 entries).

Substantial non-narrative blocks: Key Takeaways (5 bullet points), Regression Test table, Delta Analysis steps, Try With AI section (3 prompts), AICheck block, Looking Ahead section. Estimated narrative density 60-65%, below the 80% target.

expectations.text: At least 2 pushback exchanges where James resists before reaching conclusions himself
expectations.evidence: Exchange 1: James says Draft 3 is 'obviously better' and Emma challenges with 'Does a longer email prove someone communicates better?' Exchange 2: James discovers Framework-Induced Overreach in his own regulatory chain and pushes back on the framework itself: 'So the cascade map format itself pushed me to fake expertise I don't have?'
Emma says 'Mine was embarrassingly bad, actually. I scored everything as structural because I didn't understand the distinction yet.' Clear admission of past inadequacy.

expectations.text: No Emma monologue exceeds 4 consecutive sentences without James reacting
expectations.evidence: Emma's longest uninterrupted block is 3-4 sentences in the Personal Feedback Loop section. James interjects with PDCA analogy. No monologue exceeds 4 sentences.

expectations.text: James uses at least 1 business analogy and 1 thinking-out-loud fragment
expectations.evidence: Business analogy: 'In operations, we called this a PDCA cycle. Plan, Do, Check, Act.' Also references Lean, Six Sigma, OKRs from his logistics career. Thinking-out-loud: 'I keep looking at my map and my revised map and I can't tell if I actually got better at thinking or if I just got better at drawing maps.'

expectations.text: Emma uses at least 1 Socratic question and 1 visual/spatial metaphor
expectations.evidence: Socratic question: 'Does a longer email prove someone communicates better?' Visual/spatial metaphor: 'Think of it like a building renovation. Surface change is repainting the walls. Structural change is moving the load-bearing walls.'
No clear Emma exit-and-return. Emma is present throughout the lesson. James does have independent moments of discovery but Emma does not physically leave and come back.

expectations.text: Every technical concept has a standalone name findable without dialogue
expectations.evidence: Concepts have headers/bold names: 'Thinking Snapshot' (h3), 'Delta Analysis' (h2), 'Framework-Induced Overreach' (bold), 'Personal Feedback Loop' (h2). All findable via scanning.

expectations.text: The lesson includes a Try With AI section
expectations.evidence: Try With AI section with 3 prompts: Delta Analysis Assistant, Feedback Loop Builder, The Honest Adversary. Each with copy-paste prompt and learning explanation.
